issues.problem: Headline plus item 1 ('Start high-dose glucocorticoid immediately') tells readers to start steroid on suspicion. EULAR abstract recommends immediate high-dose GC in ACTIVE GCA and confirmation of a suspected diagnosis; it does not say start before confirmation. The evidence record flags this qualification. The post title says the same ('Suspected active GCA: steroid now').
issues.source_says: We recommend that a suspected diagnosis of LVV should be confirmed by imaging or histology. High dose glucocorticoid therapy (40-60 mg/day prednisone-equivalent) should be initiated immediately for induction of remission in active giant cell arteritis.
issues.replacement: Active giant cell arteritis: EULAR recommendations

issues.problem: Source gives 40-60 mg/day prednisone-equivalent; wording implies one named drug.
issues.replacement: 40 to 60 mg a day of prednisolone or equivalent

issues.text: Small studies in care homes found wax needing removal in more than half of residents, and hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.
issues.problem: Hearing improvement was measured in only one study (29 new admissions to a US skilled nursing facility); plural 'studies' overstates the evidence for the hearing outcome. Same wording in threads, bluesky and visual_text.
issues.source_says: Moore 2002: 29 residents; hearing improved in 80% of impacted ears vs 3% of nonimpacted. Morley 2019: 57% of 51 residents had excess cerumen requiring removal.
issues.replacement: Small studies in care homes found wax needing removal in more than half of residents. In one small study, hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.

issues.text: In small care home studies, hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.
issues.problem: Only one study measured hearing after removal.
issues.replacement: In one small care home study, hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.

issues.text: In small care home studies, over half of residents had wax needing removal, and hearing improved in most blocked ears once it was removed.
issues.problem: Only one study measured hearing after removal.
issues.replacement: In small care home studies, over half of residents had wax needing removal. In one, hearing improved in most blocked ears once it was removed.

issues.text: Small care home studies: wax needing removal in more than half of residents; hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.
issues.replacement: Small care home studies: wax needing removal in more than half of residents. One study: hearing improved in most blocked ears after removal.
